messages:
laura: Customer on Private (VPC) reporting intermittent TLS failures when calling embeddings via their corp gateway. Error in app logs: \"tls: handshake failure: no shared cipher\". Started after their gateway patch last night.

customer-eng: Repro notes from customer: client -> F5 APM (corporate gateway) -> our Private egress. Calls to https://private-infer.redwood.svc.local:443 fail ~30% of the time, otherwise OK. Bypass gateway and traffic succeeds.

mike: Ask them for a packet capture of the initial ClientHello. Also need exact F5 build + OpenSSL version. If they're on OpenSSL 1.0.x that could explain stripping/rewriting of TLS extensions.

customer-eng: They attached partial pcap showing ClientHello length mismatch and proxy logs with: \"SSL_read: no shared cipher\" and \"client hello truncated\" messages. Gateway vendor: F5 APM 12.1.0, OpenSSL 1.0.2k-ish. They also said security team enabled a legacy-crypto profile last night.

alan: This matches a classic case: older TLS stacks or middleboxes that try to be strict about extension parsing will truncate or drop unknown extensions (supported_versions, key_share). If key_share or supported_versions get truncated, TLS1.3 can't negotiate and some servers error out with \"no shared cipher\" because the ClientHello is malformed for TLS1.3, not because ciphers actually differ.

laura: Can we reproduce quickly? mike, can you simulate with a simple proxy that strips beyond N bytes of ClientHello?

mike: Repro locally: run a TCP proxy that cuts ClientHello after 200 bytes then pipe to our endpoint. openssl s_client -connect <proxy>:443 -tls1_3 shows handshake alert: protocol version. With -tls1_2 it succeeds.

mike: Example curl from their jump host (through gateway):
```
$ curl -Iv --http2 https://private-infer.redwood.svc.local/health
* Connected to private-infer.redwood.svc.local (10.20.30.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 (INTERNAL), Cipher unknown
* error:1409442E:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert protocol version
* Closing connection 0
```

laura: Good. Mitigations: ask customer to relax gateway rewrite/strip rules or upgrade OpenSSL on F5. If they can't upgrade, we can offer two short-term workarounds:
1) Force TLS 1.2 from the initiating side so ClientHello omits TLS1.3 extensions.
2) Route specific egress to a bypass that doesn't inspect TLS.

customer-eng: They cannot upgrade OpenSSL for ~3 weeks. Need a quick change on Redwood Private agent to restore service.

alan: We have an agent-side knob that can limit the outbound TLS max version. It's usually env-configured in the agent service. Proposed immediate instruction (different var name to be safe with existing docs):
```
# on private agent host
sudo sed -i 's/^tls_max=.*/tls_max=1.2/' /etc/redwood/agent.conf || echo 'tls_max=1.2' >> /etc/redwood/agent.conf
sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent
# then test
curl -v --tlsv1.2 https://private-infer.redwood.svc.local/health
```
This forces TLS1.2 for agent-initiated outbound connections and should avoid the broken ClientHello extensions. Warn customer this reduces security posture vs TLS1.3.

laura: I also recommended they test by switching one backend route at a time. If this fixes it, we'll add a KB entry and propose an agent feature to auto-detect truncation and fallback.

mike: Logged reproducible detection heuristic: if agent sees repeated 40x TLS alerts with ClientHello length metadata mismatch, set a local flag and retry with TLS1.2 for that host/route. We can prototype telemetry that reports the exact ClientHello len from the pcap and the parsed len post-proxy.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0456 created and assigned to laura. Priority: low/medium (customer can do workaround).

customer-eng: Customer applied tls_max=1.2 change and restarted agent. Initial smoke tests show health endpoints become consistently OK. They will run full traffic tonight and confirm.

laura: If customer confirms, we'll update support playbook: title=\"F5/APM OpenSSL 1.0 client-hello truncation -> TLS1.2 workaround\" with steps to mitigate and recommended permanent fix (upgrade/allow extensions). Also flag eng for agent auto-fallback feature.

mike: Long term: agent should emit a warning when it detects malformed/truncated ClientHello and offer an automatic rollback to TLS1.2 for the affected route plus telemetry to alert customer about middlebox behaviour.

customer-eng: Will post pcap and F5 log extracts later. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
